articles.title: Field Notes From the Spanish General Strike
articles.author: Kit Wainer
articles.content_excerpt: The November 11 Spanish general strike was the product of social movement protests around the cost of living that have been bubbling for at least two years. Housing rights struggles have sprung up around the country, as rising real estate values combined with low salaries have made rents nearly unaffordable for much of the working class. Housing unions began discussing calls for a general strike at least a year ago. It was the September 23 eviction of Maricarmen Abascal at age 87 that sparked outrage throughout the country. Her death less than two weeks later galvanized calls for the general strike. Most of the union federations got on board after the movement agreed to demand both lower rents and higher salaries. articles.title: Pregnant Workers Say Amazon Is Violating Their Rights
articles.author: Jenny Brown
articles.content_excerpt: Willamina Barclay was working as a picker at Amazon’s fulfillment center in Rochester, New York, when she felt lightheaded again. “She pleaded with a manager for a seat. . . . He refused: ‘No, because you don’t have a [pregnancy] accommodation. If I give you a chair, I have to give everybody else a chair,’” he said, according to a recent lawsuit. But Barclay, who learned she was pregnant in March 2025, had already asked managers many times for accommodations — a seat, extra breaks to drink, eat, pee (or throw up) in the bathroom, no ladder-climbing or squatting, and no heavy lifting. Amazon — a company known for fast delivery — had failed to answer for weeks, demanding medical documentation.
